To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the availability of large area, gap-free, annual time series data has the potential to significantly improve land cover mapping accuracy and consistency, 2) the inclusion of time series information in the mapping process provides information to support the development of land cover change detection algorithms and products and, 3) the inclusion of change information in the mapping algorithm supports the development of land change products that can be used to inform land cover change algorithms.
Optical remotely sensed time series (RTS) data are increasingly being used for land cover classification, and the use of RTS data is becoming a common practice.

1) The use of time-series information is essential for land cover classification and change detection; 2) The use of change information is essential for the generation of annual land cover maps; 3) Change detection methods can be used for land cover classification, but the use of time series information is essential for robust land cover classification
In summary, our research is concerned with

how time series EO data and other data sources can be integrated into land cover products, how these data products can be validated, and how the products can be used to inform land cover change detection and monitoring.
the development and application of methods to improve the accuracy and utility of land cover products for science, monitoring and reporting.
the development of land cover classification approaches that are informed by time series information, and the development of methods for assessing and improving land cover classification accuracy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

time series data can provide valuable information to improve land cover classification, however, there are a number of challenges that need to be addressed to fully realize the potential of time series data for this purpose.
there is a need for a comprehensive, multi-disciplinary review of the current status of land cover mapping, including the use of time series data, and the identification of research gaps.
time series data are a valuable source of information for informing land cover mapping.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a need for a robust approach to land cover characterization and classification, that incorporates both temporal information, and other ancillary data sources, to produce annual land cover information that can be used for a range of applications.
the incorporation of time series information in land cover mapping has the potential to improve the accuracy and utility of the products.
the use of time series data is an essential component of the land cover characterization process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
time series data are now available to enable the development of annual, large scale, land cover maps.
time series data can be used to inform land cover mapping and change detection, and can also be used as inputs to the land cover characterization process.
time series informed land cover classification has the potential to provide a robust and consistent approach for land cover characterization and monitoring.
